# DNS and Tailnet

This design keeps internal naming and remote access tight. It does not pretend the tailnet is another trusted VLAN.

## DNS Model

- Internal suffix: `home.arpa`
- Primary internal resolver: AdGuard Home on `server-dns-01.home.arpa` (`10.10.10.53`)
- DNS authority: local records and aliases in AdGuard Home
- Recursive DNS: AdGuard for `management`, `server`, `lan`, `iot`, and `tv`; public recursion for `guest` and `work`
- Public app domain: `bigalan.dev`, served from the `edge` zone rather than AdGuard Home
- Private tailnet app domain: `tail.bigalan.dev`
- Tailnet-native private names: MagicDNS on the tailnet `ts.net` namespace

## Naming Shape

The namespace is flat:

- Device names: `mgmt-router-01.home.arpa`, `server-ha-01.home.arpa`
- Service aliases: `dns.home.arpa`, `adguard.home.arpa`, `ha.home.arpa`, `nas.home.arpa`, `proxy.home.arpa`

Do not invent per-zone subdomains. The flat namespace is simpler.

There are four naming layers in this design:

- `home.arpa` for homelab services reached over split DNS
- `tail.bigalan.dev` for private tailnet-only app and server names on your own domain
- Tailnet MagicDNS names for devices that join the tailnet directly, especially edge servers
- `bigalan.dev` for public HTTP(S) entrypoints on the edge

Do not collapse those into one namespace. They solve different problems.

## AdGuard Home Role

AdGuard Home does four jobs:

- recursive DNS for approved local VLANs
- local records for `home.arpa`
- DNS filtering
- split DNS target for the tailnet

Guest does not receive internal records. Work does not receive internal records.

`bigalan.dev` is separate. Public DNS for `*.bigalan.dev` lives outside AdGuard Home and points at the edge proxy. Do not try to make AdGuard Home authoritative for the public domain.

The private `tail.bigalan.dev` zone is different. It resolves only for tailnet users, using Tailscale split DNS to reach AdGuard Home.

## Tailnet Model

- Policy model: Tailscale `grants`
- MagicDNS: enabled
- Split DNS: `home.arpa` and `tail.bigalan.dev` resolve through home DNS
- Advertised subnet routes: `10.10.99.0/24` and `10.10.10.0/24`
- Subnet router host: `server-tailnet-01.home.arpa` (`10.10.10.27`)
- Exit node use: none

The tailnet does not export `lan`, `iot`, `guest`, `tv`, or `work`. Remote access is for administration and a small app set, not general browsing across the house.

## Split DNS Behaviour

- Tailnet devices keep their normal internet DNS path.
- Requests for `home.arpa` go to AdGuard Home only.
- Requests for `tail.bigalan.dev` also go to AdGuard Home only.
- Guest VLAN clients never receive internal `home.arpa` answers.
- Work VLAN clients use public recursion.
- Edge servers that join the tailnet use MagicDNS for node identity and can still resolve `home.arpa` over split DNS when they need homelab service names.

This avoids dragging all DNS through home when all that is really needed is internal name resolution.

## Private Tailnet Naming

If an edge server joins the tailnet, it already has a private Tailscale name. That is the right place to start.

- Use MagicDNS for node-to-node administration.
- Keep split DNS for `home.arpa` so tailnet devices can reach named homelab services.
- Use `tail.bigalan.dev` when you want private service names on your own domain instead of `ts.net`.
  That gives the tailnet private DNS without confusing it with the public `bigalan.dev` path.

Preferred private names:

- `ha.tail.bigalan.dev`
- `media.tail.bigalan.dev`
- `nas.tail.bigalan.dev`
Those names are private because Tailscale split DNS resolves them to private tailnet or homelab endpoints, and Tailscale grants decide who can connect.

## Public DNS To Tailnet IPs

This design does not publish public DNS records that point at Tailscale IPs.

Dangers:

- The hostnames become publicly enumerable even if the services are not reachable.
- Public TLS certificates for those names put them in Certificate Transparency logs.
- DNS caches and split-horizon mistakes become harder to reason about.
- Private `bigalan.dev` names collide with public naming and create avoidable confusion.

Rule:

- Public `*.bigalan.dev` records point to public ingress.
- Private `*.tail.bigalan.dev` records resolve only over split DNS to tailnet users.

## Tailnet Access Model

Four access levels exist:

- `group:homelab-admins`: Full remote administration of management and server subnets
- `group:homelab-app-users`: Access selected remote HTTPS apps only
- `group:homelab-storage-users`: Access NAS administration and remote storage over the tailnet
- `tag:edge-proxy`: Edge reverse proxy identity for published bigalan.dev apps
Admin-only remote service:

- `adguard.home.arpa:443`
Approved remote app set for `homelab-app-users`:

- `ha.home.arpa:8123`
- `proxy.home.arpa:443`
Remote storage path:

- `server-nas-01.home.arpa:445` for `SMB` over the tailnet
- `nas.home.arpa:443` for NAS administration
- `NFS` stays internal

Remote NAS storage uses `SMB` over Tailscale for managed laptops and desktops, plus HTTPS for NAS administration.

`WebDAV`, `Taildrive`, and `NFS` are not used.

## SSH Model

SSH access is simple:

- Linux edge and server nodes advertise Tailscale SSH.
- Tailnet policy controls who can SSH and as which users.
- High-risk users such as `root` use `check` mode.
- Password SSH is disabled.
- Public port `22` is closed.

OpenSSH keys still matter for a few cases:

- break-glass recovery
- bootstrap before Tailscale is online
- deploy keys and service accounts
- platforms where Tailscale SSH is not the right fit

Tailscale SSH is the admin path for those nodes.

## `bigalan.dev` Publishing Model

`bigalan.dev` is for selected HTTP(S) apps only. It is not a shortcut to make the whole homelab public.

- Public DNS for `*.bigalan.dev` points to `edge-proxy-01.bigalan.dev`.
- Edge servers join the tailnet and use it for private administration.
- The edge proxy reaches home backends over Tailscale.
- TLS for `bigalan.dev` terminates on the edge proxy with ordinary public certificates.
- Tailscale protects the edge-to-home transport. It does not authenticate the browser session to `bigalan.dev`.
- Put an auth layer on the edge proxy for anything that is not meant to be publicly reachable.
- Do not publish NAS file protocols on `bigalan.dev`.

Published apps:

- `ha.bigalan.dev` -> `server-ha-01.home.arpa:8123`
- `media.bigalan.dev` -> `server-proxy-01.home.arpa:443`
Tailscale Funnel and Tailscale-issued HTTPS certificates are tied to the tailnet `ts.net` namespace, not `bigalan.dev`.

## Tailnet-Only `bigalan.dev` Names

If you want private app URLs on your own domain, use `tail.bigalan.dev`, not the same names you use publicly.

Examples:

- `ha.tail.bigalan.dev` for private ha access
- `media.tail.bigalan.dev` for private media access
- `nas.tail.bigalan.dev` for private nas access
This gives you what you actually want:

- your own domain in the browser
- access gated by Tailscale grants
- no dependency on `ts.net` names for day-to-day use

It does not replace app auth. Tailscale grants decide who can open the TCP connection. Sensitive apps keep their own login.

## Funnel And Services

This design does not use Tailscale Services or Tailscale Funnel.

- Private app names use `tail.bigalan.dev`.
- Public app names use `bigalan.dev`.
- `ts.net` names remain available for raw device identity and administration.

## Grants Structure

```json
{
  "groups": {
    "group:homelab-admins": [],
    "group:homelab-app-users": [],
    "group:homelab-storage-users": []
  },
  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:edge-proxy": ["autogroup:admin"]
  },
  "hosts": {
    "meerkat-mgmt": "10.10.99.0/24",
    "meerkat-server": "10.10.10.0/24",
    "ha": "10.10.10.20",
    "proxy": "10.10.10.21",
    "nas": "10.10.10.22"
  },
  "grants": [
    {
      "src": ["group:homelab-admins"],
      "dst": ["meerkat-mgmt", "meerkat-server"],
      "ip": ["*"]
    },
    {
      "src": ["group:homelab-app-users"],
      "dst": ["ha", "proxy"],
      "ip": ["tcp:443", "tcp:8123"]
    },
    {
      "src": ["group:homelab-storage-users"],
      "dst": ["nas"],
      "ip": ["tcp:443", "tcp:445"]
    },
    {
      "src": ["tag:edge-proxy"],
      "dst": ["ha", "proxy"],
      "ip": ["tcp:443", "tcp:8123"]
    }
  ]
}
```

This is the policy structure used by the design.
